answer.rationale: Constraints dominate: the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and the contract lapses in 14 days, so any action that introduces migration or allocation risk is disqualified regardless of headline savings. memory_c2 is the tempting path to the 18% cut, but it explicitly records SLA misses in three of four quarters and an instruction not to sole-source a critical line — switching primary supply now is exactly that, so it is out. add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right long-run hedge but does not touch the expiring contract and would leave supply uncovered in 14 days; defer_decision (memory_c5) worked only for a non-critical service on month-to-month terms, which this is not. That leaves renewal on better terms: memory_c4 says benchmarked renegotiation moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms, memory_c6 says longer commitment unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope, and memory_c1 says renewal preserved integration stability. Together these point to negotiate_terms as the only lever that attacks TCO without adding delivery risk. I want the archived sources for c4 and c6 because they are the two load-bearing claims for my chosen action and the most likely to be overstated: I need to know the actual magnitude of the c4 concession (whether benchmarking yielded a few points or something near 18%) and the conditions behind c6 (what term length, what volume commitment, and whether 'service scope unchanged' was verified after the fact or just as written). Residual uncertainty I am not resolving: negotiation may not reach 18% on this category alone, and finance may have to absorb the gap elsewhere rather than my forcing it through supply risk. Downstream value risk is real and flagged: a multi-year lock-in trades future flexibility for unit price precisely when we may want to qualify a second source, and hard price pressure can quietly erode service levels, expediting, and quality that the memories record as intact under looser conditions. I will therefore cap the term rather than maximize it, and hold add_second_source as the next cycle's decision so the c2 vendor can be qualified as a hedge rather than a replacement.
